newsitem.title: USA: White separatists indicted in U.S. bank robberies.
newsitem.headline: White separatists indicted in U.S. bank robberies.

text.p: Five members of the Aryan Republican Army white separatist group were indicted by a federal grand jury on Thursday on charges of conspiracy to rob banks to fund the group, prosecutors announced.

The five are accused of carrying out seven bank robberies in Ohio, Missouri, Iowa and Wisconsin in 1994 and 1995 and using the proceeds to buy weapons and fund recruiting efforts. All five were in custody, including their leader Mark Thomas, who surrendered on Thursday, FBI spokeswoman Linda Vizi said.
Thomas was being held in Allentown, Pennsylvania, near the group's headquarters at Macungie.

One of those named in the indictments, Michael William Brescia, has been named in a private wrongful death suit brought by a mother of two vicitms of the 1995 Olkahoma City federal building bombing. Brescia, a part-time student at LaSalle University in Philadelphia, was arrested on Thursday on the conspiracy charges. The others already were in custody.
Vizi said the bank robbery investigation had nothing to do with the Oklahoma City probe and there was nothing in the indictment to connect Brescia with the April 19, 1995 bombing.

A news release from the U.S. Attorney's office described the Aryan Republican Army as a "white separatist group," but the indictment did not characterise the group. Press reports called it part of a closely linked network of white-power, anti-government groups that includes the Aryan Nations.

One of those indicted carried a pamphlet called "New ID in Zoglandia." ZOG, or Zionist Occupation Government, is a term commonly used by right-wing extremists to refer to the U.S. government, which they regard as illegitimate.

Brescia's name was added last year to a civil suit filed by Edye Ann Smith, the mother of two children killed in the Oklahoma City blast, against suspect Timothy McVeigh. The suit alleges Brescia, Michael Fortier and Andreas Strassmeir, a German national, helped McVeigh plan and execute the bombing.

It said Strassmeir and Brescia roomed together at a white separatist compound in Oklahoma called Elohim City and were seen at parties with McVeigh. Strassmeir has denied any connection to the bombing.
